reason: The enclosure is the only offered action, and it seems suited to taking a small sample while keeping the body cold.
expectation: I expect to prepare or remove an end section for warming tests, though the exact result is unclear.

effect: The end section is available for testing while the body-bearing ice remains in its refrigerated case.
reaction: It's reassuring that the sample was taken well away from the body.
reason: The temperature stage is the only offered combination and should let me test what the sampled ice loses as it warms.
expectation: I expect the section to warm under observation and reveal some change, though I don't know what it will lose.

effect: The test showed that material can move within the ice by minus 30 even while it looks solid, so preserving the body also means keeping its surrounding layer colder than that.
reaction: I was surprised that the layer changed while the ice still looked solid.

mostWorthwhile.text: Warming the adjacent section was most worthwhile because it revealed a preservation problem that appearances alone would not show.

leastWorthwhile.text: Removing the sample was a necessary preparation, but it offered less discovery than the warming test.

surprise.text: Fine pockets began changing and material moved between grains at minus 30, before the piece visibly melted.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: taking a distant sample and testing it both served the stated goal, although each was the only combination offered.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the body and its surrounding ice are kept cold for the journey to Earth, though this chapter offered little choice in how to investigate.
